input.question: How come drinking salt water dehydrates you, but having a salt/water mix in a saline IV hydrates you? Why don’t they just use regular water?
input.ground_truth: It depends on how salty the water is. The saline in IV bags has the same salinity as human blood. Drinking beverages with the proper amount of electrolytes will not dehydrate you(Gatorade for example). Using pure water in IV bags would dilute your blood and cause complications. Drinking sea water, which has way higher salinity than human blood dehydrates you because the increase in sodium causes more water to be excreted as urine.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: How come drinking salt water dehydrates you, but having a salt/water mix in a saline IV hydrates you? Why don’t they just use regular water?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine you’re a little plant, and you need water to grow. But if you pour salty water on the plant, the salt can hurt it and make it lose the water it already has. That’s kind of like what happens to you when you drink salt water—your body doesn’t like the extra salt, so it tries to get rid of it by making you pee out more water than you drank. That’s called getting dehydrated.

But when doctors give you a saline IV, they put just the right amount of salt and water into your body, in a safe way. It’s like giving the plant exactly the right kind of water with just a tiny bit of salt, so it helps your body work better, not worse. Your body needs a little bit of salt to be healthy, but too much salt makes you lose water.

They don’t use just plain water for IVs sometimes because your body needs a special mix of salt and water to stay healthy and work the right way. If you only got plain water, it could mess up the balance of salt in your body, which is very important!
